summary: First full-stack test pass of NusaFreight ERP. Backend: created pytest suite (6 files, 94 tests) covering auth/RBAC, customers + sales data isolation, quotation totals & execute, job-order CS-vs-Finance field RBAC, shipment status, documents auto-rename, schedule-arrive H-2, invoices/PPN/coretax XML/SOA, kurs & weekly-price upsert, partners, pricing LCL & import-tax calcs, trucking RBAC, customs docs, admin users CRUD, audit logs, and role dashboards. 90/94 passing (95.7%) after I fixed 3 real ObjectId serialization 500s. Frontend: verified login (manual + one-tap demo) for admin/sales/cs/finance/pricing/customs, RBAC sidebar per role, admin customer create, quotation modal live total (1000 -> 1,100 with 10% margin), import tax calc, LCL calc (200 USD), trucking/weekly tabs, invoice list + Coretax XML export toast, kurs save, partner/SOA pages, CS job order page (finance fields correctly hidden), customs page. Found 1 CRITICAL frontend data-isolation bug (React Query cache not cleared between users) and 1 missing client-side route guard.

minor.issue: Unknown job_order_id returns 200 {ok:true} (silent no-op $push). Should 404. Same pattern in PATCH /api/job-orders/{id}, PATCH /api/customs-docs/{id}, POST /api/invoices/{id}/mark-paid, POST /api/schedule-arrive/{id}/confirm — none verify the document exists.
No brute-force lockout: 6+ consecutive wrong passwords all return 401, no 423/429 and no attempt counter.
No httpOnly cookie is set; JWT is returned in body only and stored in localStorage (XSS-exposed). get_current_user already reads a cookie named access_token, so the cookie path is dead code.
Not implemented (405). No delete/deactivate for master customers — test data and mistakes cannot be removed.
Endpoint does not exist (only GET). Review request listed 'POST /api/audit-logs must be admin/finance only'; if writes are intended it is missing.
Seed only inserts admin when absent; changing ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env never updates the existing admin hash (playbook expects idempotent update).
allow_origins=['*'] + allow_origin_regex='.*' together with allow_credentials=True. Wildcard + credentials is invalid per spec; CORS_ORIGINS from .env is never read. Use explicit origins.

No per-sales data isolation — a sales-owned job order/invoice is visible to every CS/finance/customs user. Acceptable for internal ops but inconsistent with the isolation applied to customers/quotations; confirm intent.

ui_bugs.issue: No client-side RBAC route guard. Logged in as CS, navigating directly to /admin/users renders the full 'User & Role Management' page with an enabled 'New User' button (list is empty because the API 403s). Same for /finance/invoice, /pricing etc. Should redirect or render 403.
data-testid is derived from the label (`demo-adminowner`, `demo-customerservice`) instead of the role (`demo-admin`, `demo-cs`) as documented. Inconsistent/undiscoverable test ids.

integration_issues.flow: Logout -> login as a different role (SPA, no page reload)
integration_issues.issue: CRITICAL data leak: the React Query cache is never cleared on logout/login (index.tsx staleTime=30s, no queryClient.clear() in auth.logout/login). After logging out of admin and logging in as sales@nusafreight.com, /master/customer showed 'Customers (20)' including customers owned by Admin (Owner)/other sales, and the Dashboard rendered the admin-only KPIs (Job Orders, Outstanding/Collected invoice amounts, Customs Pending/Cleared) for the Sales user. A hard reload as sales correctly shows 'Customers (7)' and only quotation/arrival KPIs, proving the backend is correct and this is purely client cache reuse across identities. Fix: call queryClient.clear() (or removeQueries) inside logout() and after successful login().

issues: The user/logout footer uses `absolute bottom-0 w-64` but the parent <aside> has no `relative`, so it positions against the initial containing block; on short viewports with a long menu it can overlap nav items. Add `relative` to the aside.

No loading skeletons or error states on any list page — useQuery isLoading/isError are unused, so a failed API call silently renders an empty table (visible on CS -> /admin/users which shows 'Users (0)' instead of an access-denied message).

action_items: CRITICAL: clear the React Query cache on logout and on login (queryClient.clear()) in /app/frontend/src/store/auth.tsx — currently a Sales user sees the previous Admin session's customers and finance/customs KPIs.
Add a role-aware route guard in App.tsx (map route -> allowed roles, redirect/403 otherwise) so CS cannot open /admin/users.

Return 404 when the target document does not exist in PATCH /api/job-orders/{id}, POST /api/job-orders/{id}/shipment-status, PATCH /api/customs-docs/{id}, POST /api/invoices/{id}/mark-paid, POST /api/schedule-arrive/{id}/confirm (use matched_count).

Auth hardening: httpOnly cookie for the JWT, failed-login counter + lockout, idempotent seed_admin that re-hashes when ADMIN_PASSWORD changes, and explicit CORS origins from CORS_ORIGINS instead of '*' with allow_credentials.
Add DELETE (or soft-delete) for /api/customers; decide whether POST /api/audit-logs is required.
Add loading/error states to list pages and rename login demo test ids to demo-<role>.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: insert_one() mutates the passed dict by adding a BSON _id; create_customer forwarded that same dict to audit(), so every GET /api/audit-logs returned 500 ('ObjectId is not iterable'). I added an _id filter inside audit(); prefer passing copies or explicitly whitelisted change dicts.

server.py upsert_kurs / upsert_weekly_price returned `{**existing, ...}` straight from find_one (with _id) -> 500 on the update path. Fixed with strip(); adopt the rule that every find_one must use projection {'_id': 0}.

auth.tsx: token in localStorage + global axios.defaults means any XSS steals a 12h admin token, and no per-user query key means cached data crosses identities. Consider scoping query keys with user.id in addition to clearing the cache.
server.py is 1029 lines in one file — split into routers (auth, customers, quotation, job_order, finance, pricing, customs, admin) before it grows further.
Dashboard/list pages ignore useQuery isLoading/isError; add explicit states so 403/500 responses are visible to the user instead of rendering an empty table.

rca_of_the_issue: 1) GET /api/audit-logs, POST /api/kurs (update path) and POST /api/weekly-prices (update path) returned 500 with ValueError: [TypeError("'ObjectId' object is not iterable")]. Root cause: Motor's insert_one mutates the input dict by injecting a BSON ObjectId under '_id'; create_customer then persisted that mutated dict into audit_logs.changes, and the two upsert endpoints echoed a find_one result that still carried '_id'. FastAPI's jsonable_encoder cannot serialize ObjectId. Fixed by stripping '_id' in audit() and by using strip() on the echoed existing docs, plus a one-off script to repair the 9 already-poisoned audit_logs rows. Verified: 47/47 finance+pricing+admin tests pass afterwards. 2) Sales user seeing Admin's 20 customers and finance/customs KPIs: reproduced only on SPA navigation, never after a hard reload — root cause is the shared React Query cache (queryKey ['customers'], ['dashboard'], ['users'] with staleTime 30s) that is never invalidated when the identity changes in auth.tsx logout()/login(). Backend isolation is provably correct (pytest asserts every returned customer has sales_id == the sales user's id).
